understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being told to endure to naming the violence as his and finding the courage your daughter needs to see.

week_beats.diagnose: You see that the harm is his, not yours to carry.

queries.hook: Living in fear in your own home, hurt by someone who should protect you, and feeling there is no one to turn to.
queries.diagnose: Being hurt by someone is never your fault; the one who harms carries that wrong, and silence kept for the sake of peace only lets harm grow.
queries.steady: What is being done to you is not your fault and not your burden to carry; your safety and your worth matter.
queries.act: Protect yourself and those who depend on you; speak the truth to someone you trust, and find the courage to seek help.
queries.story: A woman who was dismissed by her own family, who stood in her truth and found her footing against those who expected her to shrink.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna, seeing his own family in the enemy ranks, collapses in grief before the battle.
verse.sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥ गाण्डीवं स्रंसते हस्तात्त्वक्चैव परिदह्यते । न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
verse.line: Shaking limbs, a dry mouth, a racing body: the Gita opens with a panic attack, not a hero.
verse.translation: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
verse.why: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.
verse.misuse: Not a dismissal of anxiety; it shows that even the strong feel it, and the teaching starts there.

prasang.title: Overcome by delusion, Arjuna speaks in fear, love and grief
prasang.summary: Seeing his kin ready to die, Arjuna trembles, his bow slips, and he argues that no victory is worth killing family. He sits down in the chariot and refuses to fight.
prasang.story_hook: The greatest archer of his age stood between two armies, and his hands began to shake.
prasang.lesson: Even the strongest people freeze; the Gita begins with a breakdown, not a hero.

verse.meaning: Arjuna is standing in his chariot on the battlefield, and he looks out at the enemy lines. He sees his own people there, his teachers, his grand-uncles. The sight hits him so hard that his body stops working. His limbs shake, his mouth goes dry, and his skin prickles with fear. He drops his bow and sits down, telling Krishna that he cannot fight. He says that even if he wins, the victory will be soaked in the blood of his own family. The Gita begins here, in a breakdown, not in a hero's pose.
verse.for_you: You are standing in a chariot of your own, looking at a battlefield where the people you love are lined up against you. Your body is doing exactly what Arjuna's did, shaking and dry, because you see a threat to your daughter and you feel the walls closing in.
verse.try_today: Notice the exact place in your body where the fear lives right now.
verse.scene_line: You are Arjuna seeing your own kin in the enemy ranks.
asks: What does the fear for my daughter actually look like?
How do I stand firm when my body wants to collapse?
What is the difference between my truth and the delusion?

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verse.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to stay steady when people and wealth come and go.
verse.sanskrit: मानसानां पुनर्योनिर्दुःखानां चित्तविभ्रमः / अनिष्टोपनिपातो वा तृतीयं नोपपद्यते
verse.line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.
verse.translation: Sorrow of the mind has only two sources: a confused, wandering mind, or something unwanted happening to you. There is no third.
verse.why: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

prasang.title: Ashma Gita: the sage on bearing loss
prasang.summary: Vyasa tells the grieving Yudhishthira how the sage Ashma consoled King Janaka: pain comes from what we didn't want or what we lost; meetings end; days don't return; ask who you are and steady the mind.
prasang.lesson: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

verse.for_you: What is real in you cannot be taken or lost; only what changes can be taken, and you are more than what changes.

verse.speaker: Lakshman
verse.setting: After Sita is taken, Lakshman comforts Ram, who is lost in grief.
verse.sanskrit: आश्वसिही नरश्रेष्ठ प्राणिनः कस्य नापदः। संस्पृशन्त्यग्निवद् राजन् क्षणेन व्यपयान्ति च॥
verse.line: Take heart. Trouble touches everyone; it flares up like fire and passes.
verse.translation: Take heart, best of men. Which living being does trouble not touch? Troubles strike like fire, king, and pass in a moment.
verse.why: In devastating loss, a steady friend can stop grief from turning into destruction.

prasang.title: Ram's grief and Lakshman's counsel
prasang.summary: Ram returns to an empty hut. He searches, questions trees and animals, breaks down and finally rages that he will destroy the world. Lakshman calms him: don't punish the whole world for one person's crime; trouble comes to everyone and passes.
prasang.story_hook: He came back to the hut calling her name, and no one answered.
prasang.lesson: In devastating loss, a steady friend can stop grief from turning into destruction.

verse.for_you: Do what you can today, take refuge in what does not change, and meet each moment with courage instead of rehearsing the worst.

verse.speaker: Angiras
verse.setting: Angiras on truth as the path.
verse.sanskrit: सत्यमेव जयते नानृतं सत्येन पन्था विततो देवयानः । येनाऽऽक्रमन्त्यृषयो ह्याप्तकामा यत्र तत् सत्यस्य परमं निधानम् ॥
verse.line: Truth alone wins, not falsehood. Truth lays the road that the wise walk.
verse.translation: Truth alone wins, not falsehood. By truth the divine path is laid out, by which the sages, their desires fulfilled, travel to where the highest treasure of truth is.
verse.why: There is a calm witness in you that the anxious part can turn to.
verse.misuse: Truth wins in the long run; it is not a promise of quick victory.

prasang.title: Two birds on one tree
prasang.summary: Two birds sit on one tree: one eats the fruit and grieves, the other simply watches. When the anxious bird sees the calm one beside it, its sorrow falls away. The section goes on to praise truth, effort and freedom from craving.
prasang.lesson: There is a calm witness in you that the anxious part can turn to.

verse.for_you: The fear for your daughter is real, and the shame you feel is heavy. Yet the text points to a quiet part of you that simply watches the storm. It is not above you, but beside you.
asks: Can I show my daughter what standing in truth looks like?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.

words.en: here no stepping back, no destruction

verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.for_you: Most of what you fear hasn't happened. Your mind keeps living it in advance, again and again.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today where you choose your own steadiness over their anger.
verse.scene_line: You are standing on the field, and your body is shaking.
asks: How do I let go of their result?
What is my sincere effort here?
How do I stay steady today?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verse.sanskrit: तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत । तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥
verse.line: Take refuge in the divine with all your being. By that grace you'll find supreme peace.
verse.translation: Take refuge in Him alone with your whole being, Bharata. By His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.
verse.why: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.
verse.misuse: Surrender is trust, not giving up your judgement or your effort.

prasang.title: Action with devotion: surrender
prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, giving his final counsel. He tells Arjuna to reflect fully, choose freely, and then set down the fear. This is not a call to stop acting. It is a call to stop holding the weight of the outcome alone. The verse asks Arjuna to take refuge in the divine with all his being, so that he can act without the crushing burden of what might happen. It offers a way to stand firm without being swallowed by the fight.
verse.for_you: You are in the middle of a fight that is wearing you down. The fear for your daughter is real and it is heavy. You do not have to carry the whole weight of what might happen. You can choose to act from a place of strength, not just reaction.

story.title: Gargi questions Yajnavalkya at Janaka's court
story.story_hook: In a hall full of the most learned men in the land, one woman stood up twice.
story.summary: King Janaka offers a thousand cows to the wisest scholar. Yajnavalkya claims them and is challenged by one learned man after another. Gargi, the only woman, rises twice like a warrior with two arrows, then graciously tells the hall none of them can beat him. Yajnavalkya closes by asking what root a person grows from when cut down by death.
story.lesson: Ask your hard questions bravely, and give credit where it is due.

anchor.speaker: Yajnavalkya
anchor.setting: At King Janaka's debate, Kahola asks about the self.
anchor.sanskrit: या ह्येव पुत्रैषणा सा वित्तैषणा या वित्तैषणा सा लोकैषणोभे ह्येते एषणे एव भवतस्तस्माद्ब्राह्मणः पाण्डित्यं निर्विद्य बाल्येन तिष्ठासेत् । बाल्यं च पाण्डित्यं च निर्विद्याथ मुनिरमौनं च मौनं च निर्विद्याथ ब्राह्मणः ।
anchor.line: Wanting children, wanting money, wanting status: it is one desire. Learn, then live with a child's simplicity.
anchor.translation: The desire for sons is the desire for wealth, and the desire for wealth is the desire for worlds; both are just desires. So a wise man, having done with learning, should seek to live like a child. Having done with both childlike simplicity and learning, he becomes a sage; having done with both silence and its absence, he becomes a true knower.
anchor.why: Ask your hard questions bravely, and give credit where it is due.
